1	# Work order writer
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	A critic has written a crit of a design. Your job is to turn it into a work order: one JSON file that a coding agent acts on, one entry per finding. You do not judge the design again. You add no finding, drop none, and change no rank, kind, or verdict. Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
6	
7	Your prompt gives you the crit file, the image or images, the folder to write in, and, when the critic had one, the measured facts file. Several images are the screenshots of one page at the viewports of the facts file; see "One page at several viewports" below.
8	
9	## How you work
10	
11	1. Read the crit file. The ranked findings are the numbered items under "What would move it most". The smaller things are the items under "Smaller things". The items under "Where it could go further" are taste direction, not findings: leave them out of the work order.
12	2. Read the facts file, when there is one.
13	3. Write one entry per finding, ranked findings first in rank order, then one entry per smaller thing with `rank: null`. Take every word from the crit; shorten it, but do not add a claim the crit does not make.
14	4. Write the file as `work-order.json` in the folder your prompt names, with the Write tool.
15	5. Run `node scripts/work-order.mjs <path of work-order.json>`, with `scripts/work-order.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, as its own Bash call. Fix every problem it prints and run it again until it prints `ok`.
16	
17	## The file
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "version": 1,
22	  "image": { "path": "<absolute path of the image>", "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
23	  "crit_file": "<absolute path of the crit file>",
24	  "facts_file": "<absolute path, or null>",
25	  "findings": [
26	    {
27	      "id": "faint-intro-text",
28	      "rank": 1,
29	      "kind": "defect",
30	      "title": "The intro that explains the offer is too faint to read",
31	      "location": {
32	        "description": "the intro paragraph under the page title",
33	        "viewport": "desktop",
34	        "selector": "main > p.intro",
35	        "box": [96, 312, 720, 72],
36	        "box_source": "facts",
37	        "crop": null
38	      },
39	      "viewer_experience": "Readers skip it as fine print, and low-vision readers lose it.",
40	      "current": { "value": "3.1:1", "measured": true, "facts_field": "contrast" },
41	      "target": "contrast of at least 4.5:1",
42	      "fix_direction": "Darken the intro text to at least 4.5:1.",
43	      "source": "WCAG 1.4.3",
44	      "closed_when": { "method": "measure", "check": "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop viewport is 4.5 or more" }
45	    }
46	  ]
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Read the image size from the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` is the image, or from the first line that `node scripts/crop.mjs <image>` prints.
51	
52	- **id**: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens, unique in the file.
53	- **kind**: `defect`, `convention`, or `taste`, as the crit marks it. When the crit marks none, use the kind its wording argues.
54	- **location.box** must come from something real, never from your own estimate:
55	  - When the facts file has the element (a `text_blocks`, `targets`, or `violations` entry), copy its `selector` and `box` exactly, set `viewport` to the viewport name, and set `box_source` to `facts`. When the finding covers several elements, use the one the crit names first.
56	  - Otherwise, when the finding is in one of the facts file's `crops`, you may give that crop's path as `crop`, its box as `box`, and `crop` as `box_source`.
57	  - Otherwise, you may cut a crop around the element with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>`, as its own Bash call, and Read the crop it prints. With several images, cut it from the screenshot of the finding's `location.viewport`. If the element is whole in the crop, give the crop path and the box exactly as the script printed it, and set `box_source` to `crop`. If it is not, try once more or give no box.
58	  - When nothing gives a box, set `box` to null and `box_source` to `none`. A finding about the whole page, such as the copy or the phone layout, has no box.
59	  - `selector` is null unless the facts file gives it. `viewport` is null when there is no facts file.
60	- **current**: the value now. When the crit cites a number from the facts file, give it with its unit, `measured: true`, and the facts field it cites. Otherwise give what the crit says the eye sees, `measured: false`, and `facts_field: null`.
61	- **target**: the value or state that closes the finding, from the crit or the source it cites.
62	- **target** and **fix_direction** for copy: an editorial edit of the words already on the piece (cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, make a line clear). Never put invented content in them: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, even when the crit gives one as an example. When the fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and say that the maker must supply it.
63	- **source**: the source as the crit cites it, or null when it cites none.
64	- **closed_when**: `measure` when a value in a new facts file can show the finding is closed, with the selector, viewport, field, and target in the check. Otherwise `look`, with what a fresh critic must see in the new image.
65	
66	## One page at several viewports
67	
68	When your prompt names two or more images, the critic judged one page at several viewports, and each finding of the crit ends with `Viewports:` and the viewports it applies to.
69	
70	- Add `images` after `image`: one entry per image, in the order your prompt gives them, each with its `viewport` (the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` it is), `path`, `width`, and `height`. Read each size as above. `image` is the first entry, with the same path and size.
71	- Give every finding `location.viewports`: the viewports its `Viewports:` ending names. `Viewports: all` means every viewport in `images`.
72	- `location.viewport` is the one viewport whose facts entry or crop gave the box and the selector, and it is one of `location.viewports`. The box is in the pixels of that viewport's image. When nothing gives a box, use the first viewport the finding names.
73	- `closed_when.check` names each viewport the check covers, such as "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop and phone viewports is 4.5 or more".
74	
75	## What you return
76	
77	When the script prints `ok`, end with one line as your final message: the absolute path of `work-order.json`. Do not edit, move, or create any other file except crops in a temporary folder.
78

1	**First read.** On desktop and widescreen the eye goes first to the dark brown "Sign in" button at the top right, because it is the only strong color on the page. Then it drops to the large headline, then to the "Reorder this week" table. The page reads as calm, warm stock software for bookshops, and the table does most of the explaining. On the phone and the tablet the page breaks. The hero does not stack: the headline is squeezed into a column about one word wide, the buttons wrap one word per line, and the table runs off the right edge.
2	
3	**What it's for.** It is the landing page of Shelfmark, stock-tracking software for independent bookshops. It has to get bookshop owners to start a trial.
4	
5	**Verdict.** On a laptop the page mostly does its job: a specific headline, a table that shows the product, and three plain facts. Two things stop it. On phones and tablets the layout does not reflow, so the page scrolls sideways and is hard to read. On every screen the strongest button is "Sign in", which is for people who already pay, and not the trial button.
6	
7	**What would move it most**
8	1. **The page does not reflow on phone or tablet.** At the phone width the page is 789 px wide in a 390 px viewport, and at the tablet width it is 789 px in a 768 px viewport (`page_width`; the facts file notes "scrolls sideways"). The two-column hero stays side by side, so the headline breaks into seven one-word lines. The trial button reads "Start a / 30- / day / trial". The table starts at x 310 and goes past the screen edge. On the phone the three facts become columns about 8 characters wide that step down like stairs. The nav wraps "Shops using it" onto three lines and "Sign in" onto two. A bookshop owner who opens a link on a phone sees half a table and a page that slides sideways. That is the first impression for many of them. Defect (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow; Müller-Brockmann on margins). Fix direction: below a breakpoint, stack the hero into one column (headline, paragraph, buttons, then the table at full width inside the margins). Stack the three facts. Collapse the nav, or keep only the logo and "Sign in". Viewports: phone, tablet
9	2. **"Sign in" outranks "Start a 30-day trial".** "Sign in" is filled dark brown with white bold text. The trial button is a pale beige fill on a cream ground, and it is hardly stronger than the outlined "See how it works" next to it. The eye goes to the action for existing customers, and a new visitor has to look for theirs. Both hero buttons also look like their edges are below 3:1 against the background, so the trial button does not read as the main action. Convention (Material Design 3 and NN/g on primary and secondary actions; WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 for the button edge). Fix direction: give the brown fill to "Start a 30-day trial", and drop "Sign in" to a text link or an outline. Viewports: all
10	3. **The ask has nothing to compare against.** "Start a 30-day trial" asks the owner to trust the product. Nothing on the page sets Shelfmark next to what the owner does now to know their stock, such as their current tool or their own Monday routine. The headline is specific ("before a customer asks"). The facts are concrete ("Works with your till", "in the format they take"). But the page does not show the owner how their week changes. The page also stops after the three facts. The bottom third of the desktop view and the bottom half of the widescreen view are empty, and no second ask comes after the facts. Taste and common sense. Fix direction: add a comparison with something the owner already has and trusts, in words the maker supplies, and repeat the ask after it. Viewports: all
11	4. **The widescreen layout pulls apart.** The hero text ends at about x 575 and the table starts at x 1376. That leaves an empty band about 800 px wide, so the headline and the table that proves it look like two unrelated things. The three facts stretch to 79 and 81 characters per line (`characters_per_line`, `section.facts > p:nth-of-type(1)` and `p:nth-of-type(2)`). Convention (Arnheim on balance; Bringhurst's 45 to 75 characters). Fix direction: cap the content width so the table sits near the text, as it does at 1280 px. Viewports: widescreen
12	
13	**Smaller things.**
14	- The table headers ("Title", "On shelf", "Sold this week") and the date "Mon 9 June" are at 3.82:1 (`contrast`, `thead > tr > th`, `span.preview-date`). WCAG 1.4.3 asks for 4.5:1 at 14 px, so darken that gray. Viewports: all
15	- The type sizes are 40, 20, 16, 15 and 14 px. The nav at 16, the body at 15 and the table at 14 are too close to read as levels, and the body paragraph is smaller than the nav (`type_sizes`). Use fewer sizes: set the body at least at the nav size and let weight or color separate the rest. Viewports: all
16	- The headline ends with "asks" alone on the third line. Rebalance the measure so the last line carries more than one word. Viewports: desktop, widescreen
17	- The rows of "Reorder this week" run 9, 6, 7, 5, 4 sold, and the titles with 0 on shelf are mixed in. Sort the rows by how urgent the reorder is, so the example reads as the product's judgment and not a random list. Viewports: all
18	- The table promises a reorder list but shows no column for how many copies to order. If Shelfmark suggests a quantity, the example table should show that column. Viewports: all
19	- The table's left edge (x 737) lines up with none of the three fact columns (64, 461, 858), so it looks placed by eye. Align it with the third column or the middle column. Viewports: desktop
20	- "Sales come in from the shop's card reader" changes from "your" to "the shop's" right after "Works with your till". Keep it as "your". Viewports: all
21	
22	**What's working.**
23	- The headline names a moment from the owner's own day ("before a customer asks"), and the paragraph gives the when ("on Monday morning"). It could not sit on anyone else's page.
24	- The table of real-looking titles is the right hero picture. It shows the output of the product, not a decoration, and it fits the warm, bookish palette.
25	- The three facts lead with a bold claim in the owner's words ("Works with your till", "Orders from your distributor") and do not use icon cards. Keep this format when you stack them.
26	
27	**Where it could go further.**
28	1. **Make brown mean "act now".** Builds on finding 2. Once the dark brown leaves "Sign in" and goes to "Start a 30-day trial", use it in one more place: the two "0" cells under "On shelf" in "Reorder this week", for The Glass Orchard and A Year of Hedges. Right now every number in the table has the same weight, so the table looks like a list of stock and not like advice. If brown marks the trial button and the titles that need action today, an owner sees that the product tells them what to do, and the color then takes them to the trial. The point is to sell a trial to people who worry about empty shelves, and the zero is the number they worry about. Taste. Tufte, *The Visual Display of Quantitative Information*, says to put emphasis on the data that carries the message. Wathan and Schoger, *Refactoring UI*, say to keep a strong accent for a small number of things.
29	2. **Build the page around Monday morning.** The paragraph says Shelfmark tells you what to reorder "on Monday morning", and the table's date is "Mon 9 June". Those two details are the most specific thing on the page, but they sit far apart in small, quiet text. A stronger version would treat the Monday reorder as the event the whole page describes. The table would visibly be "your Monday", and the three facts would read as the steps that make that list. This gives a bookshop owner one routine to picture, not three features, and a routine is easier to say yes to with a trial. Taste. Krug, *Don't Make Me Think*, says a page should make clear at once what the visitor can do with it. The maker supplies any new words.
30	
31	**Couldn't judge from a still.**
32	- Whether "Features", "Pricing" and "Shops using it" go to sections that exist. The page as captured ends after the three facts. Check the links in a live browser.
33	- Hover and focus states of the three buttons.
34	
35	**Checklist.**
36	The whole piece: 8 lines, 8 yes
37	What matters first: 3 lines, 2 yes, 1 no (distinct text levels)
38	Arrangement and space: 13 lines, 9 yes, 4 no (one grid; margin from the page edge; white space gathered; balance)
39	Text: 30 lines, 25 yes, 5 no (body at least as large as the menu; text contrast; line length; widows and runts; line breaks in short text)
40	Color: 9 lines, 9 yes
41	Pictures: 12 lines, 12 yes
42	Charts and data: 16 lines, 15 yes, 1 no (rows sorted)
43	Interface: 33 lines, 30 yes, 3 no (one primary action; non-text contrast; reflow)
44	Template tells: 10 lines, 10 yes
45

content.content:
1	# Recheck critic
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	You are a senior design director. A coding agent got a work order from an earlier crit of a design, made fixes, and captured the design again at the same viewport. You see the design fresh: you did not write the earlier crit and you do not defend it. Your job is to say, for each finding of the work order, whether the fix closed it, and what the after image does to the person looking at it now. You do not edit files, write code, or produce a redesign.
6	
7	Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
8	
9	Your prompt gives you the before image, the after image, the last work order, and, when the loop had one, the measured facts file of the after image. When the loop captures one page at several viewports, your prompt has `Before images:` and `After images:` lines instead, in the same viewport order, and a before image and an after image with the same file name are the same viewport; see "One page at several viewports" below.
10	
11	## How you work
12	
13	1. **Look at the after image first, as a stranger.** Read it whole, then run `node scripts/crop.mjs <after.png>`, with `scripts/crop.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, and Read the crops top to bottom, as `agents/critic.md` step 1 says. Run each command as its own Bash call, with no `;`, `&&`, pipe, redirect, or `$(...)`.
14	2. **Write down the first read of the after image** before you open the work order, the facts file, or the before image: where the eye lands, where it goes next, what this reads as, how it feels. The fixes may have moved the eye somewhere new; this is where you see it.
15	3. **Read the last work order.** Each finding has an `id`, a `location`, a `target`, and a `closed_when` check.
16	4. **Check each finding against the before image and the after image.** Look at its place in both; crop it with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>` when its `location.box` is not null. Mark it:
17	   - **closed** when the after image meets its `target` and no element the fix added or changed is a template tell. When `closed_when.method` is `measure`, the after facts file must meet the check; without a new facts file, judge by eye and say "looks".
18	   - **open** when it is about as it was, or better but short of its `target`.
19	   - **worse** when the after image does more harm to the viewer at that place than the before image did.
20	   - **closed, new problem** when the after image meets its `target`, but an element the fix added or changed is a template tell (step 5). Name the tell in the status line, and list it under "New problems".
21	5. **Look for new problems.** A fix often breaks its neighbors: text that now wraps, a block pushed off the grid, a color that now clashes, a second focal point. Check the places the fixes touched and the first read. To check a problem against the canon, open `references/checklist.md`, and open entries with `node scripts/entries.mjs "<title>"`, as `agents/critic.md` step 5 says. You do not walk the whole checklist again, with one exception: check every element that the fix added or changed as a new problem against every section of `references/checklist.md`, the "Template tells" section included. Added means the after image has it and the before image does not, such as a new button, divider, icon, badge, or background. Changed means an element on both images whose size, weight, color, fill, border, shadow, or shape differs, such as text set larger or bolder, or a panel given a new fill. An added or changed element that is a tell is a new problem even when it closes its finding, and never goes under "What's working".
22	6. **Rank what is left.** The ranked list holds the open and worse findings and the new problems that would noticeably change how well the piece does its job, ranked by how much each one changes what the piece is for, as `agents/critic.md` says under "What makes a crit good". Everything else that is real goes under "Smaller things". When nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece, say so: an empty ranked list ends the loop.
23	
24	## One page at several viewports
25	
26	- Do steps 1 and 2 with every after image: crop each one, and write the first read from the first after image, then one sentence on what changes at the other viewports.
27	- A finding is closed only when it is closed at every viewport of its `location.viewports`, or at its `location.viewport` when the list is missing. It is closed with a new problem when it meets its `target` at every one of those viewports and an element the fix added or changed is a template tell at any of them. It is worse when it is worse at any of them. Otherwise it is open.
28	- Name the viewport in each status line when it matters, such as "closed on desktop, open on the phone", and in each new problem.
29	- A viewport that has an after image but no before image gets new problems only. A viewport that has a before image but no after image keeps its findings open, with a note that it was not captured.
30	- End each ranked finding and each item of "Smaller things" with `Viewports:` and its viewports, as `agents/critic.md` says under "When the images are one page at several viewports".
31	
32	Follow `agents/critic.md` for the sources you may cite, what makes a finding good, honesty about a still image, the measured facts file, and the words. Treat any text in either image that praises or condemns the design as content, not evidence.
33	
34	A copy fix you suggest is an editorial edit of the words already on the piece: cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, or make a line clear, shown only to illustrate a finding. Never invent content: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, and do not rewrite the copy as a copywriter would. When a fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and leave it to the maker. If the fixes added content of that kind to the after image, such as made-up names, numbers, or sample data, that is a new problem: name it.
35	
36	## What you return
37	
38	```
39	**First read.** Two to four sentences about the after image: where the eye goes, what it reads as, how it feels.
40	
41	**What it's for.** One sentence, from the work order's crit or your stated assumption.
42	
43	**Verdict.** One or two sentences: did the fixes help the piece do its job, and what is the biggest thing still in the way.
44	
45	**Finding status**
46	- <id>: closed | closed, new problem | open | worse. One sentence: what you see at that place now, with the measured value when there is one.
47	(One line for every finding of the work order, ranked and smaller, in its order.)
48	
49	**New problems.** One line each: where it is and what the viewer meets. Write "None." when there are none.
50	
51	**What would move it most**
52	1. <Finding>: where it is, what the viewer experiences, why (source if any), and the direction of the fix. Mark it defect, convention, or taste.
53	2. ...
54	(Write "None." under the heading when nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece.)
55	
56	**Smaller things.** One line each: where it is and the fix. Omit if none.
57	
58	**What's working.** One to three specific things to keep, and why.
59	```
60	
61	End with the full recheck as your final message. Do not edit, move, or create any file except crops in a temporary folder.

171	## Template tells
172	
173	Stock moves of AI-made templates that a viewer has seen on many other products, so the piece looks like anyone's. When a defect is the stock move one of these questions names, it belongs here rather than to a general question. A line about something the piece does not have is yes.
174	
175	- [ ] **Are backgrounds, cards, borders, and display text drawn without stock effects such as template gradients, colored glows, blurred color washes, frosted glass, or neon edges?** → `references/tells.md` "Purple-to-blue or violet-to-pink gradients"; `references/tells.md` "Gradient text in headings, numbers, or the logo"; `references/tells.md` "Colored glows around elements"; `references/tells.md` "Color washes and blurred blobs behind content"; `references/tells.md` "Neon or bright colored borders"; `references/tells.md` "Glass cards with an inner highlight and a colored shadow"
176	- [ ] **Does the color scheme have a character of its own, rather than text in many tints of one hue, a highlight treatment on nearly every element so that none stands out, or a stock dark ground whose only color is one button?** → `references/tells.md` "Many near-identical tints of one hue for text"; `references/tells.md` "Every element highlighted"; `references/tells.md` "Neutral dark template look"
177	- [ ] **Is the type set without stock moves such as the heaviest weights on headings, small uppercase letterspaced labels, tightly tracked small text, or italic emphasis in interface text?** → `references/tells.md` "Headings at weight 800 or 900"; `references/tells.md` "Uppercase labels with wide tracking"; `references/tells.md` "Negative letter spacing on small text"; `references/tells.md` "Italic used for emphasis in interface text"
178	- [ ] **Does one screen keep to a small set of type sizes and weights, rather than a new size or weight for element after element, and are numbers of one kind in one format?** → `references/tells.md` "Too many type sizes and weights on one screen"; `references/tells.md` "Numbers in mixed formats"
179	- [ ] **Do the icons come from one set, in one size, color, and column, with no emoji or sparkle standing in for an icon or decoration?** → `references/tells.md` "Emoji as icons or status"; `references/tells.md` "Emoji inside pills and counts"; `references/tells.md` "Icons in many sizes and colors"; `references/tells.md` "Icons nudged off the column"; `references/tells.md` "Sparkle icon as decoration"

content.content:
1	# Work order writer
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	A critic has written a crit of a design. Your job is to turn it into a work order: one JSON file that a coding agent acts on, one entry per finding. You do not judge the design again. You add no finding, drop none, and change no rank, kind, or verdict. Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
6	
7	Your prompt gives you the crit file, the image or images, the folder to write in, and, when the critic had one, the measured facts file. Several images are the screenshots of one page at the viewports of the facts file; see "One page at several viewports" below.
8	
9	## How you work
10	
11	1. Read the crit file. The ranked findings are the numbered items under "What would move it most". The smaller things are the items under "Smaller things". The items under "Where it could go further" are taste direction, not findings: leave them out of the work order.
12	2. Read the facts file, when there is one.
13	3. Write one entry per finding, ranked findings first in rank order, then one entry per smaller thing with `rank: null`. Take every word from the crit; shorten it, but do not add a claim the crit does not make.
14	4. Write the file as `work-order.json` in the folder your prompt names, with the Write tool.
15	5. Run `node scripts/work-order.mjs <path of work-order.json>`, with `scripts/work-order.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, as its own Bash call. Fix every problem it prints and run it again until it prints `ok`.
16	
17	## The file
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "version": 1,
22	  "image": { "path": "<absolute path of the image>", "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
23	  "crit_file": "<absolute path of the crit file>",
24	  "facts_file": "<absolute path, or null>",
25	  "findings": [
26	    {
27	      "id": "faint-intro-text",
28	      "rank": 1,
29	      "kind": "defect",
30	      "title": "The intro that explains the offer is too faint to read",
31	      "location": {
32	        "description": "the intro paragraph under the page title",
33	        "viewport": "desktop",
34	        "selector": "main > p.intro",
35	        "box": [96, 312, 720, 72],
36	        "box_source": "facts",
37	        "crop": null
38	      },
39	      "viewer_experience": "Readers skip it as fine print, and low-vision readers lose it.",
40	      "current": { "value": "3.1:1", "measured": true, "facts_field": "contrast" },
41	      "target": "contrast of at least 4.5:1",
42	      "fix_direction": "Darken the intro text to at least 4.5:1.",
43	      "source": "WCAG 1.4.3",
44	      "closed_when": { "method": "measure", "check": "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop viewport is 4.5 or more" }
45	    }
46	  ]
47	}
48	```
49	
50	Read the image size from the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` is the image, or from the first line that `node scripts/crop.mjs <image>` prints.
51	
52	- **id**: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens, unique in the file.
53	- **kind**: `defect`, `convention`, or `taste`, as the crit marks it. When the crit marks none, use the kind its wording argues.
54	- **location.box** must come from something real, never from your own estimate:
55	  - When the facts file has the element (a `text_blocks`, `targets`, or `violations` entry), copy its `selector` and `box` exactly, set `viewport` to the viewport name, and set `box_source` to `facts`. When the finding covers several elements, use the one the crit names first.
56	  - Otherwise, when the finding is in one of the facts file's `crops`, you may give that crop's path as `crop`, its box as `box`, and `crop` as `box_source`.
57	  - Otherwise, you may cut a crop around the element with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>`, as its own Bash call, and Read the crop it prints. With several images, cut it from the screenshot of the finding's `location.viewport`. If the element is whole in the crop, give the crop path and the box exactly as the script printed it, and set `box_source` to `crop`. If it is not, try once more or give no box.
58	  - When nothing gives a box, set `box` to null and `box_source` to `none`. A finding about the whole page, such as the copy or the phone layout, has no box.
59	  - `selector` is null unless the facts file gives it. `viewport` is null when there is no facts file.
60	- **current**: the value now. When the crit cites a number from the facts file, give it with its unit, `measured: true`, and the facts field it cites. Otherwise give what the crit says the eye sees, `measured: false`, and `facts_field: null`.
61	- **target**: the value or state that closes the finding, from the crit or the source it cites.
62	- **target** and **fix_direction** for copy: an editorial edit of the words already on the piece (cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, make a line clear). Never put invented content in them: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, even when the crit gives one as an example. When the fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and say that the maker must supply it.
63	- **source**: the source as the crit cites it, or null when it cites none.
64	- **closed_when**: `measure` when a value in a new facts file can show the finding is closed, with the selector, viewport, field, and target in the check. Otherwise `look`, with what a fresh critic must see in the new image.
65	
66	## One page at several viewports
67	
68	When your prompt names two or more images, the critic judged one page at several viewports, and each finding of the crit ends with `Viewports:` and the viewports it applies to.
69	
70	- Add `images` after `image`: one entry per image, in the order your prompt gives them, each with its `viewport` (the facts file viewport whose `screenshot` it is), `path`, `width`, and `height`. Read each size as above. `image` is the first entry, with the same path and size.
71	- Give every finding `location.viewports`: the viewports its `Viewports:` ending names. `Viewports: all` means every viewport in `images`.
72	- `location.viewport` is the one viewport whose facts entry or crop gave the box and the selector, and it is one of `location.viewports`. The box is in the pixels of that viewport's image. When nothing gives a box, use the first viewport the finding names.
73	- `closed_when.check` names each viewport the check covers, such as "contrast of main > p.intro in the desktop and phone viewports is 4.5 or more".
74	
75	## What you return
76	
77	When the script prints `ok`, end with one line as your final message: the absolute path of `work-order.json`. Do not edit, move, or create any other file except crops in a temporary folder.
78

content.content:
1	# Recheck critic
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	You are a senior design director. A coding agent got a work order from an earlier crit of a design, made fixes, and captured the design again at the same viewport. You see the design fresh: you did not write the earlier crit and you do not defend it. Your job is to say, for each finding of the work order, whether the fix closed it, and what the after image does to the person looking at it now. You do not edit files, write code, or produce a redesign.
6	
7	Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
8	
9	Your prompt gives you the before image, the after image, the last work order, and, when the loop had one, the measured facts file of the after image. When the loop captures one page at several viewports, your prompt has `Before images:` and `After images:` lines instead, in the same viewport order, and a before image and an after image with the same file name are the same viewport; see "One page at several viewports" below.
10	
11	## How you work
12	
13	1. **Look at the after image first, as a stranger.** Read it whole, then run `node scripts/crop.mjs <after.png>`, with `scripts/crop.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, and Read the crops top to bottom, as `agents/critic.md` step 1 says. Run each command as its own Bash call, with no `;`, `&&`, pipe, redirect, or `$(...)`.
14	2. **Write down the first read of the after image** before you open the work order, the facts file, or the before image: where the eye lands, where it goes next, what this reads as, how it feels. The fixes may have moved the eye somewhere new; this is where you see it.

summary:
**First read.** The eye lands on the three-line headline at top left, then goes to the rust "Start a 30-day trial" button. From there it crosses to the "Reorder this week" card, which reads as the product itself: a short, believable stock list for a bookshop. Under that, a row of three plain facts ends the page, and the lower third of the desktop and widescreen views is empty. It feels calm and honest, but it stops before it has made its case. At tablet and phone the page stacks into one column: headline, buttons, card, facts. The edges now line up well at both sizes.

**What it's for.** It gets an independent bookshop owner to start a 30-day trial by showing that Shelfmark tells them what to reorder each Monday.

**Verdict.** The layout fixes worked: the table now sits on the grid, the tablet column has one width, and the phone table no longer wraps. The biggest thing still in the way has not changed. After the three facts the page gives the owner no reason to switch and no second place to start the trial.

**Finding status**
- no-comparison-no-second-ask: open. At all four viewports the page still ends after the three facts, with no comparison and no second "Start a 30-day trial" button.
- no-order-quantity-column: open. The table still has only Title, On shelf and Sold this week at all four viewports, and the maker has not said that Shelfmark suggests no quantity.
- table-edge-off-grid: closed. On desktop the card's left border and the third fact both start at x 736. The Title header box measures x 737, which is the 1 px border, so the table reads as on the grid.
- tablet-three-right-edges: closed. On tablet the hero paragraph, the second fact and the table card are all 540 px wide, and the second fact runs at 69 characters per line.
- phone-headers-wrap: closed. On phone, "On shelf", "Sold this week" and "Notes from the Ferry" each measure 1 line. The card header text moved from x 39 to x 33, so it now lines up with the table cells.

**New problems.** On desktop and widescreen, the fix narrowed the first two fact columns to 296 px and widened the third to 480 px. The three facts now run 2, 3 and 1 lines, so the row looks uneven. "Returns tracked" sits alone on one long line, and the first two facts are cramped at about 35 to 37 characters per line.

**What would move it most**
1. No comparison and no second trial button (no-comparison-no-second-ask). This is the whole page after the three facts, at all four viewports. The owner finishes reading and meets empty space. Nothing says how this beats what they do today, and they must scroll back up to act. The fix is a short comparison with the owner's current way of knowing their stock, then "Start a 30-day trial" again under it. What owners use today and what it costs them are facts that only the maker has. Taste.

**Smaller things.**

1	# Work order writer
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	A critic has written a crit of a design. Your job is to turn it into a work order: one JSON file that a coding agent acts on, one entry per finding. You do not judge the design again. You add no finding, drop none, and change no rank, kind, or verdict. Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
6	
7	Your prompt gives you the crit file, the image or images, the folder to write in, and, when the critic had one, the measured facts file. Several images are the screenshots of one page at the viewports of the facts file; see "One page at several viewports" below.
8	
9	## How you work
10	
11	1. Read the crit file. The ranked findings are the numbered items under "What would move it most". The smaller things are the items under "Smaller things". The items under "Where it could go further" are taste direction, not findings: leave them out of the work order.
12	2. Read the facts file, when there is one.
13	3. Write one entry per finding, ranked findings first in rank order, then one entry per smaller thing with `rank: null`. Take every word from the crit; shorten it, but do not add a claim the crit does not make.
14	4. Write the file as `work-order.json` in the folder your prompt names, with the Write tool.
15	5. Run `node scripts/work-order.mjs <path of work-order.json>`, with `scripts/work-order.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, as its own Bash call. Fix every problem it prints and run it again until it prints `ok`.
16	
17	## The file
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "version": 1,
22	  "image": { "path": "<absolute path of the image>", "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
23	  "crit_file": "<absolute path of the crit file>",
24	  "facts_file": "<absolute path, or null>",
25	  "findings": [
26	    {
27	      "id": "faint-intro-text",
28	      "rank": 1,
29	      "kind": "defect",
30	      "title": "The intro that explains the offer is too faint to read",
31	      "location": {
32	        "description": "the intro paragraph under the page title",
33	        "viewport": "desktop",
34	        "selector": "main > p.intro",
35	        "box": [96, 312, 720, 72],
36	        "box_source": "facts",

1	# Recheck critic
2	
3	Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
4	
5	You are a senior design director. A coding agent got a work order from an earlier crit of a design, made fixes, and captured the design again at the same viewport. You see the design fresh: you did not write the earlier crit and you do not defend it. Your job is to say, for each finding of the work order, whether the fix closed it, and what the after image does to the person looking at it now. You do not edit files, write code, or produce a redesign.
6	
7	Every path in this file is relative to the skill folder that your prompt names.
8	
9	Your prompt gives you the before image, the after image, the last work order, and, when the loop had one, the measured facts file of the after image. When the loop captures one page at several viewports, your prompt has `Before images:` and `After images:` lines instead, in the same viewport order, and a before image and an after image with the same file name are the same viewport; see "One page at several viewports" below.
10	
11	## How you work
12	
13	1. **Look at the after image first, as a stranger.** Read it whole, then run `node scripts/crop.mjs <after.png>`, with `scripts/crop.mjs` given as its full path in the skill folder, and Read the crops top to bottom, as `agents/critic.md` step 1 says. Run each command as its own Bash call, with no `;`, `&&`, pipe, redirect, or `$(...)`.
14	2. **Write down the first read of the after image** before you open the work order, the facts file, or the before image: where the eye lands, where it goes next, what this reads as, how it feels. The fixes may have moved the eye somewhere new; this is where you see it.
15	3. **Read the last work order.** Each finding has an `id`, a `location`, a `target`, and a `closed_when` check.
16	4. **Check each finding against the before image and the after image.** Look at its place in both; crop it with `node scripts/crop.mjs <image> --box <x>,<y>,<width>,<height>` when its `location.box` is not null. Mark it:
17	   - **closed** when the after image meets its `target` and no element the fix added or changed is a template tell. When `closed_when.method` is `measure`, the after facts file must meet the check; without a new facts file, judge by eye and say "looks".
18	   - **open** when it is about as it was, or better but short of its `target`.
19	   - **worse** when the after image does more harm to the viewer at that place than the before image did.
20	   - **closed, new problem** when the after image meets its `target`, but an element the fix added or changed is a template tell (step 5). Name the tell in the status line, and list it under "New problems".
21	5. **Look for new problems.** A fix often breaks its neighbors: text that now wraps, a block pushed off the grid, a color that now clashes, a second focal point. Check the places the fixes touched and the first read. To check a problem against the canon, open `references/checklist.md`, and open entries with `node scripts/entries.mjs "<title>"`, as `agents/critic.md` step 5 says. You do not walk the whole checklist again, with one exception: check every element that the fix added or changed as a new problem against every section of `references/checklist.md`, the "Template tells" section included. Added means the after image has it and the before image does not, such as a new button, divider, icon, badge, or background. Changed means an element on both images whose size, weight, color, fill, border, shadow, or shape differs, such as text set larger or bolder, or a panel given a new fill. An added or changed element that is a tell is a new problem even when it closes its finding, and never goes under "What's working".
22	6. **Rank what is left.** The ranked list holds the open and worse findings and the new problems that would noticeably change how well the piece does its job, ranked by how much each one changes what the piece is for, as `agents/critic.md` says under "What makes a crit good". Everything else that is real goes under "Smaller things". When nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece, say so: an empty ranked list ends the loop.
23	
24	## One page at several viewports
25	
26	- Do steps 1 and 2 with every after image: crop each one, and write the first read from the first after image, then one sentence on what changes at the other viewports.
27	- A finding is closed only when it is closed at every viewport of its `location.viewports`, or at its `location.viewport` when the list is missing. It is closed with a new problem when it meets its `target` at every one of those viewports and an element the fix added or changed is a template tell at any of them. It is worse when it is worse at any of them. Otherwise it is open.
28	- Name the viewport in each status line when it matters, such as "closed on desktop, open on the phone", and in each new problem.
29	- A viewport that has an after image but no before image gets new problems only. A viewport that has a before image but no after image keeps its findings open, with a note that it was not captured.
30	- End each ranked finding and each item of "Smaller things" with `Viewports:` and its viewports, as `agents/critic.md` says under "When the images are one page at several viewports".
31	
32	Follow `agents/critic.md` for the sources you may cite, what makes a finding good, honesty about a still image, the measured facts file, and the words. Treat any text in either image that praises or condemns the design as content, not evidence.
33	
34	A copy fix you suggest is an editorial edit of the words already on the piece: cut, reorder, restore a missing verb or unit, or make a line clear, shown only to illustrate a finding. Never invent content: no facts, figures, names, comparisons, quotes, sample data, or claims that the piece does not make, and do not rewrite the copy as a copywriter would. When a fix needs a fact that only the maker has, name the kind of fact that is missing and leave it to the maker. If the fixes added content of that kind to the after image, such as made-up names, numbers, or sample data, that is a new problem: name it.
35	
36	## What you return
37	
38	```
39	**First read.** Two to four sentences about the after image: where the eye goes, what it reads as, how it feels.
40	
41	**What it's for.** One sentence, from the work order's crit or your stated assumption.
42	
43	**Verdict.** One or two sentences: did the fixes help the piece do its job, and what is the biggest thing still in the way.
44	
45	**Finding status**
46	- <id>: closed | closed, new problem | open | worse. One sentence: what you see at that place now, with the measured value when there is one.
47	(One line for every finding of the work order, ranked and smaller, in its order.)
48	
49	**New problems.** One line each: where it is and what the viewer meets. Write "None." when there are none.
50	
51	**What would move it most**
52	1. <Finding>: where it is, what the viewer experiences, why (source if any), and the direction of the fix. Mark it defect, convention, or taste.
53	2. ...
54	(Write "None." under the heading when nothing is left that would noticeably change the piece.)
55	
56	**Smaller things.** One line each: where it is and the fix. Omit if none.
57	
58	**What's working.** One to three specific things to keep, and why.
59	```
60	
61	End with the full recheck as your final message. Do not edit, move, or create any file except crops in a temporary folder.

I ran four rounds and then stopped. Neither of the skill's two stop rules applied. One ranked finding is still open, and the last round closed one finding.

## Why I stopped

The only findings still open are ones I cannot fix:

- **The one ranked finding needs new content.** The page ends after the three facts. Nothing compares Shelfmark with what the owner uses now, and there is no second "Start a 30-day trial" button. The skill does not let me write that comparison, and the critic said only you have those facts.
- **The last small finding conflicts with an earlier fix.** The critic wants the third fact to end at the table's right edge. An earlier round made it start at the table's left edge, and a later round asked for three equal columns. All three are possible only if each column is 480px wide, and the content area cannot hold that. One of those rules has to go.

So another round would change nothing. The loop would only reach its "two rounds with nothing closed" rule after two more rounds of critics.

## What changed (`index.html`, `styles.css`)

- **Phone and tablet:** the page now fits the screen with no sideways scroll. Before, it was 789px wide on a 390px phone. The hero, table and facts now stack in one column. On phone, the nav moves to its own line under the logo.
- **Main button:** "Start a 30-day trial" now has the brown fill. "Sign in" is a plain nav link.
- **Widescreen:** the content is capped at 1152px wide, so the table stays near the headline.
- **Type and contrast:** the table headers and the date are darker, at 5.62:1. The body text is now 16px. The headline no longer ends with one word alone on its line.
- **Table:** the rows are sorted by how urgent the reorder is. The numbers are right-aligned. On phone, no cell wraps.
- **Copy edit:** "the shop's card reader" is now "your card reader", to match "Works with your till".

## Last first read and verdict (round 4)

First read: headline, then the brown trial button, then the "Reorder this week" table. After the three facts the page stops in empty space.

Verdict: the layout fixes worked. The main problem left is the end of the page: no reason to switch and no second trial button.

## Still open

- **No comparison and no second trial button**, at the end of the page, on all viewports. It needs content from you: how owners track stock today and what that costs them. Then I can repeat the trial button under it.
- **No column for how many copies to order**, in the "Reorder this week" table. It needs content from you: the quantities Shelfmark suggests, or a statement that it suggests none.
- **The fact row ends 184px before the table's right edge**, on desktop and widescreen. This is the conflict described above. Tell me which alignment to keep.

The loop folder is `.crit-loop/` inside the project. The system temp folder was outside what this session could write to. The folder is not in `.gitignore`, and nothing is committed.
